chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Tha'laba ibn Maimun, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him),
regarding His Exalted and Glorious saying: 'The Knower of the unseen and the witnessed.' He said: The unseen is what has not yet been, and the witnessed is what has already been.

key_terms.الشَّهَادَةُ: The witnessed; that which is present, visible, or has already come into existence
key_terms.الْغَيْبُ: The unseen; that which is hidden from human perception or has not yet occurred
key_terms.عَالِمُ: The Knower; one of the divine attributes referring to comprehensive knowledge
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Exalted and Glorious; an honorific title for God

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of the unseen and the witnessed in Shia tafsir?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides a concise ontological definition of divine knowledge, distinguishing between the unseen as potentiality (that which has not yet manifested) and the witnessed as actuality (that which has come to pass). This interpretation aligns with Shia theological emphasis on Allah's comprehensive knowledge encompassing both the temporal and the eternal, reinforcing the concept that nothing escapes His awareness regardless of its state of existence. Such definitions are crucial for understanding the scope of *Ilm al-Ghayb* in Shia exegesis, distinguishing it from mere prediction to a fundamental attribute of the Divine Essence.
